utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, this is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic. Good afternoon, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for having kept you waiting for so long because the previous case was not over, so we only have one sitting this afternoon, we'll sit until 7.00. Yes, Ms. Chana. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour,, good evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Marko, yesterday the last question you were asked was whether you knew Enver Buza because you heard his name spoken by someone and you said that you heard later who Enver Buza was. What did you learn about Enver Buza?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know Enver Buza myself. Only later I find out from the Croatian soldiers that he was the commander of the Prozor Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now you said you heard soldiers' voices. Can you please assist the Chamber with, again, how many voices were they and how many soldiers you saw?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw three soldiers, and I just heard one voice asking, "What are we going to do with the women and the children?"

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And did you hear a reply?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard a soldier reply, "They should kill everybody that they caught."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were they talking amongst each other or was there -- were they -- did you see any equipment, communication equipment on the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see whether they had any communication equipment. I suppose it was a Motorola they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Why do you suppose they had a Motorola?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these people asked, "What are we going to do with the women and the children?" I suppose they were not talking amongst each other but that they were asking somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you just suppose or did you see a Motorola or did you hear anything that suggested to you that it was a communication device?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see anything, but I suppose that that is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how far away you were in your hiding place from where the soldiers - excuse me - and where your family was standing?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six to seven metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, yesterday I showed you this photograph of the junction, which is MFI 357. If that could please be brought on to the screen. Is it there before you? Yes. Can you tell us on this picture, where it is that your family was standing? Is it possible? Can you see it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure the witness said they were standing anywhere. I don't think he said anything about how they were positioned. I don't object to the witness marking where they were when he last saw them, but if they were standing still or standing, then he'd better give that evidence rather than having it put to him, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, standing means they are on their feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if that's all it means -- I was really concerned with the issue of movement or stillness, frankly. With that then I took standing to mean stillness in the question that was asked. I might be wrong about that, but I know what my friend is getting at with the question. It's quite a proper question; it just had that word standing. That's what I was concerned by

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said you were in a hiding place. What was your family doing, and where were they? Can you be really quite detailed about this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my hiding place, I could not see whether they were standing or not. According to what I could hear, the conversation, I suppose that they were standing at the junction that you see before you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So just to be quite clear, you could not see them, you could just hear them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And in what direction did you hear your mother pleading, as you said, with the soldiers not to kill her from where you were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of this junction. Towards my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Okay. Then tell us, did you hear anything else, what the soldiers said, other than what you've already told this Court?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard them talking, but I cannot recall exactly what it was that they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: All right. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had heard what they were planning to do with the women and children, when I heard them say that they should kill every person that they caught, after that I heard bursts of fire as well as individual shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And you were still continuing to hide?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the soldiers after these bursts of fire? Did they talk again, did they say anything?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They talked again, but I don't know what about.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: About how many gunshots did you hear? If you can remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember with precision, but I could hear bursts of fire and individual shots being fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you, at 15 years of age, familiar with firearms yourself?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen automatic rifles carried by our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the sounds different weapons made?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were bursts of fire and individual gunshots.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And what would you attribute that noise to, what kind of weapon, if you can. What did you think the weapons were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought they were automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: When you saw the soldiers, had you seen any weapons on them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What kind of weapons were they carrying?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, they were carrying automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, did you hear any voices from your family at this time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you quite correctly. At which particular moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: After the bursts of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the bursts of fire and after the individual shots, I did not hear any voices anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, after you said the soldiers talked a little bit, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the bursts of fire and the individual gunshots, I could hear from what the soldiers were talking amongst themselves that they were going to move, that they were moving in the direction of the village and towards the school there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What is it which made you say that that's where they were moving? What did they say that you heard?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not remember exactly what it was precisely that I heard, but I heard -- I could deduct from what they were saying that they were moving away from the spot in which they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, how soon after those bursts of fire did you hear the soldiers say they are now moving? Was it immediately or did they -- was it some time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, not long after the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, after the soldiers moved away, what did you do? Mr. Marko, you take your time. Don't force yourself to say anything. If you need sometime, just take it.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went out of my hiding place and down to the road where I saw my brother and sister lying dead, and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Marko, I know this is extremely difficult for you, and that is why I'm not showing you the photographs where it actually depicts your family. But I would like you to look at MFI 357 again, please, and if you could tell us from that picture where you saw the bodies of your family. Is it possible for you to do that? If it's not, Mr. Marko, that would be perfectly all right as well. If you just draw circles and numbers. If you first tell us where your brother was, Stjepan.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would you put, in that circle, a 1, please. Or just put S for Stjepan, if that's all right, sorry. And would you now please tell us where your sister Marija's body was. Circle that and put an M inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, can you please put another circle for your mother and put an R.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marko.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'll tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P357.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marko, when you saw the bodies, and I'll only ask you about your brother Stjepan, did he have his trousers on him?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not. He only had his underwear on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you recall what happened to his trousers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Had he had them on as you were running away from the house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, what did you -- what kind of wounds did you observe on the bodies when you saw them? And we'll start with Stjepan.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see that there was blood on my brother's head around his ear.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Anything else that you noticed on your brother Stjepan? Mr. Marko, I'll just move on from this in a minute, whenever you feel you're ready to go on, and then if you feel we may revisit it or not, as the case may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might be able to assist a little bit here. Can I indicate that I was not going to cross-examine on the wounds that he observed on his siblings and his mother, and so frankly I don't mind if my friend doesn't deal with it or -- it's up to her really, but that's my indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, could we skip this part?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I had every intention to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Marko, we will not talk about this anymore and everybody entirely understands, so please do not worry about it. Now, after what happened, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went a bit farther away from my -- from the place where I had been hiding. I went away some distance, I'm not quite sure, about 100 metres away from that place. And there I stopped because I did not dare run anymore because they were shooting all around me. And I could see smoke billowing in the surrounding villages from the houses and stables that had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: How long did you continue to stay wherever you were? I presume -- you said in the forest; right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I actually spent almost a whole day on that spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: You just stayed there waiting for the fire, the firing to abate or ...

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I waited for the firing to die down so that I could move away from that place.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And did you eventually move away from that place?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went on in the direction of the village of Rajici.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came to the road, I met our soldiers and they recognised me and then they took me to the town of Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, did you return to your house sometime later?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on that day. But sometime later, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: What was the state of your house when you saw it next time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The windows of the house were shattered. When we went inside the house, we could see the effects of the two hand-grenades that had been thrown into the house, and we would see the pock-marked walls as a result of the bullets that had entered the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marko, did you have an older brother by the name of Ivan Zelic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Could you tell us what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an HVO member, and he was killed on the 24th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And in your home, did you have any weapons of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had two hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And anything else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And two grenades that remained from my late brother Ivan.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Did you ever see those grenades again?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, did you ever go back to live in your house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Marko, I would like to thank you very much for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination, please, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thanks very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: First of all, I have a question about your brother who was an army member. When he died in January of 1993, whereabouts in the house did he leave the two hand-grenades that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in our new house where the two hunting rifles were, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you came back to the village after all of these sad events, did you ever find those two hand-grenades or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My uncle came there before I did, and he took the two hunting rifles and anything of value in the house. I do not know whether the two hand-grenades were among the things he took.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What is the name of your uncle?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pavo Zelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And was Pavo, at that time, a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And on the morning when the killings took place, was Pavo on duty or was he off duty as an HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was on duty that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And based upon what you were told, whereabouts was he on duty that morning?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Zelijaca [phoen] position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is the Zelijaca position one which is about 500 meters from another HVO position called Borak?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When Pavo was off duty, in which house did he used to stay?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was that house in Zelenike village?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zelic, we've had evidence from other witnesses about the numbers of people remaining in the village of Kriz, and I'd just like to ask you a little bit about who was living in the village of Zelenike on the morning of the killings. Firstly on the morning of the 14th of September of 1993, can you recall how many men of the Zelenike village were members of the HVO, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this information precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's not an objection to this particular question. But in general I would just like to say that the boy was only 15 years old, and I think learned counsel should bear that in mind with some of the questions he's going to ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were a number of the member of the village of Zelenike members of the HVO army at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were all in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And does that -- were you aware at that time of an organisation for the older men called the home guard?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just exercising your memory as best you can now, do you recall any of the older men of the village of Zelenike performing duties such as patrolling the village streets or indeed any other such duties in early September 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, they didn't do those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just as to those two hand-grenades, when was the last time you'd seen those two hand-grenades before the killings? Had you seen them a day before, a month before, or a week before? What's your best estimate?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a month before, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Had your brother, who was in the HVO, ever explained to you how those grenades were to be used if your house or the village was attacked?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never explained that to me, nor did he ever allow me to come near them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did he ever explain to you how did -- perhaps I'll take another step. After he died, I take it you didn't have, in the family house, his personal weapon, his army rifle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. As to the hunting rifles, did he show you how to shoot those rifles?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As a 15-year-old boy, you had fired -- or I should ask you rather than putting the proposition. Had you fired either of those rifles in your life?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The Uzdol area is primarily a farming area, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And is it, in fact, an area where sometimes wild creatures will come, such as wolves?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boars, foxes, hares.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was it ever known that a bear would come to that area?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it was very common for householders to have in their house a hunting firearm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My late father had been a hunter. He had the proper licences for those rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed there was a hunting club of some sort in the village, was there not, to which the Zelenika family belonged or members of the Zelenika family belonged? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The member of the--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter was not sure. She heard the members of the Zelic family, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. Perhaps I may not have asked the question well and the interpreter had a doubt, Mr. Zelic. You'll have to forgive me I'll just ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In that hunting club were there members of the Zelenika family, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were there also members of the Zelic family, your own family?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my late father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You may have been too young at the time to know, but you may know, so I'll ask you the question: Before the hostilities broke out between the HVO and the Bosnian army, were you aware that the Uzdol hunting club had, in fact, associated in quite a friendly way with a hunting club primarily of Muslim people from the village of Scipe?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand what village you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zelic, it will be my pronunciations, no doubt. Do you know the village of Scipe, S-c-i-p-e, which is primarily a Muslim village some distance away, Scipe?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, hunters from Kute would come together with my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The hunters from Kute were primarily Muslim people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in the days before the fighting commenced between the Bosnian army and the HVO, your father, and indeed your family, had friendly relations with Muslim families from elsewhere including Kute; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Are you able to comment on this proposition? I'll put a proposition to you; you tell us if it's accurate or not. It was likely that quite a few Muslim people knew that in the houses in Uzdol, even when there weren't military people there, there might well be hunting weapons there. Are you able to comment on that proposition or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. On the morning of the killings, to your knowledge, the school in Uzdol was not operating as a school; is that correct? Rather, it was -- I'll put the question more fully. It was operating as a battalion headquarters for the 3rd Battalion of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there were soldiers there. I don't know if it was a headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But at that time of your life, you were still of school age, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had completed school some three months before in that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your younger siblings who were so sadly killed, they were not attending the school in Cer at that time, in those months, I should perhaps say; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: School-aged -- many school-aged children had been evacuated from the villages, from the hamlets around Uzdol and moved to Prozor, Rumboc or elsewhere; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it is the fact that -- I won't put the fact to you, I'll ask you. Were you told by anyone the night before the killings happened that there was the danger or the possibility of a Muslim attack, a Bosnian army attack the following morning?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On that last night before the killings, did your mother take any special steps, unusual steps concerning the security of the family?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether any ammunition or weapons were found in the proximity of your brother Stjepan's trousers when they were found later on?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you anything about that topic as to whether there was any ammunition found near those trousers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I have a couple more preliminary questions, then I'm going to turn to what you noticed when you fled, then your cross-examination will be finished. I want to indicate to you, Mr. Zelic, that I expect to finish your cross-examination tonight, and I'm intending to attempt to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, would it be appropriate to press on without a break. I'm content to do that and I think if we can do that, that would be the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we'll sit until 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The last preliminary questions are these: Did you know Janja Grubesa who lived in Zelenike?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did you know Pavo Grubesa?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Where was Pavo Grubesa living at that time, the morning of the killings, 14th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was living in Zelenike, but I don't know where he was on that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. Was he an HVO member himself?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When -- you don't know whether he was in the village that morning, I understand, but on the occasions when he did sleep in the village, did he sleep in the house of Janja Grubesa or in another house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to say who else was living in the house of Janja Grubesa on the morning of the killings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I heard, it was Janja Grubesa and Maja Zelenika. No, not Zelenika, that's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You meant Grubesa; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you know Miroslav Grubesa?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what relation was Miroslav Grubesa to Janja Grubesa?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were brother and sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How old was Miroslav Grubesa at that time, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he a friend of yours, or a neighbour and contemporary of yours?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a relative of mine and we knew each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know whether he had in his house a weapon or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I now want to move to the time when the soldiers arrived. Is it the fact that you were woken by the sound of gunfire or shots?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did the shots appear to you to be coming from any particular direction when you awoke?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shooting could be heard near the house, not from the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This courtroom is very quiet, Mr. Zelic, and it's hard to get a sense of the atmosphere at the time. Is it the fact that there was shooting or the sound of gunfire going on very consistently from the time you woke up until quite sometime after your family was killed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could hear the shooting all the time, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And did that shooting seem to come from various different places at the same time? In other words -- perhaps that's a bad question, I'll ask you another question. Did the shooting all come from the one place or did it seem to come from different places?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did you also notice some larger explosions, explosions such as would be caused by the falling of shells, mortar bombs or other such artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you notice whether any such shells landed anywhere near to you during the course of your -- of this day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Did you notice whether there was any smoke drifting around the village of Zelenike, whether it be from artillery fire or from fires at houses or buildings?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From houses on fire, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. When you woke up, did you wake up effectively to a scene of panic, with your mother urging you all to get out of the house quickly?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who exactly woke me up. And there was shooting nearby so we left the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, did you leave the house by escaping out of a window on one side of the house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any people on the other side of the house as you escaped through that window?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment I didn't, but the shooting was very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you hear any explosions close to the house such as might be caused by a hand-grenade at that time when you were about to escape or indeed when you were escaping?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you got out the window before your mother or whether she got out before you?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went out first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you observe with your own eyes whether or not your mother had with her any hand-grenades while she was still inside the house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I have to ask you a question about a particular book that's been published which has been tendered in evidence in this Court. Are you aware of a book, the text of which was written by Kazo Zelenika and the -- some form of editing was performed by Gusto Vlajcic which was entitled "Uzdol" and issued in about the year 2000 with the purpose of raising funds I think for the church or school in the village of Uzdol. Do you know that book? I think it was actually to raise funds for a memorial in the village.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that book. I've never seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If you've never seen it, I won't trouble you by showing it to you, but I have to ask you to comment on a particular passage. In that book, a claim is made that your mother bravely threw hand-grenades in order to assist the escape of the children and of herself. Now, are you able to offer any comment about that? Did your mother throw hand-grenades or a hand-grenade in order to assist the escape of the children and herself?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, she didn't throw any hand-grenades. And I don't know who wrote that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I just have to ask you some details to the best of your memory about this escape from the house. Were you the first to go out that window?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was your mother the last to come out that window?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember who jumped out after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You may not recall the precise details or the precise words, but do you recall whether your mother gave you an instruction to run in a particular direction once you got out the window? In other words, did she say, "Run to the Zelenika house," or, "Run to the school," or anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, she said, "Run to the school."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is that what you did as soon as you got out the window?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And it was after running towards the school that you came in sight of Ivan Zelenika's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is jumping ahead a little bit but it will assist us to go through the path that you ran. You jumped out the window -- I just want to put this to you, tell me if I'm right: You jumped out the window, you ran a little way until you could see Ivan Zelenika's house, after stopping there for a short period of time, you then ran in another direction towards that road junction where you ultimately hid. Is that correct? Is that the order that things took?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you ran from your house, from your window down towards the Zelenika house, were you with your little brother and sister at that time, or did they catch up to you at the place that you stopped near the Zelenika house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were behind me, about 10 metres behind me. They didn't catch up with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you able to say where, in relation to those two, your mother was on the way down from your house to the Zelenika house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, she was behind them, but I can't tell you how far behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now I want to come to what you observed at the Zelenika premises. You indicated here that you saw Ivan Zelenika standing next to a man in uniform with a gun; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At the time when you looked, you weren't sure whether that person in the uniform was from a friendly or an unfriendly military force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know who he was, I just saw that he had a weapon in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But just by looking at his uniform, you weren't able to tell which side he was on. Is that an accurate statement or not?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm putting a proposition to you, and I'm asking you to indicate whether you agree or disagree with this proposition. The proposition is: Just by looking at the uniform of this man with the weapon, you couldn't tell which side he was on. Is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't tell that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But nevertheless -- did you notice any buildings burning in the near vicinity as you made that observation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My neighbour Ivan's stable was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And can you say for how many seconds you looked at Ivan and had man as they stood six or seven metres outside his house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three, four or five seconds, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And after that, did you turn and run in a different direction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you hear any firing coming from the direction of the -- of Ivan Zelenika's house as you ran away?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, approximately how long after you started running away from you hear that noise?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately after 20 seconds or half a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: May I ask you a question: What was the stance or the position of Ivan Zelenika when you last saw him before you turned to run away?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You may or may not recall this, but I will just ask you to try: Do you recall what he was wearing when you last saw him standing outside his house?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's okay. Did you hear -- or sorry, pardon me. Did you see the face of the soldier that was standing -- I should take that back with the soldier, but the person in uniform with a gun that you saw standing near to him? Did you see that man's face? In the five seconds that you were looking?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just -- I need to ask you this question for completeness, you didn't see his face. I take it you did not recognise this individual; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, after that, you fled towards the junction and my question now is: Were you ahead of or behind your other family members?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahead of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And in the time that you -- as you were running along with your family close behind -- were they close -- do you know whether they were close behind you or can you not recall precisely where they were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment at which I could see them, I thought that they were quite close, but how close, I cannot tell you with precision at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And are you able to say when that was that you had that view of them, was it as you ran along or was it as you went to find cover in the place that you've indicated in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was running along, I turned backwards once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you -- you've indicated that you made a move to -- to hide and I just want to ask you what it was that triggered that decision to hide? Did you see some soldiers or enemy forces or did you hear some such soldiers? What was it that caused you to go where you went to hide, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall, not with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Some of the questions I ask may seem awfully obvious to you, but we do need your -- we need it to be on the record what you say about it. As you ran from the Zelenika house towards the junction, I take it your state of mind was one of extreme fear as a 15-year-old boy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And there was the sound of gunfire coming from various different parts of the Uzdol area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And some of that gunfire sounded as if it was quite close; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were unable to say -- sorry, I should take that back. You were unable to see the people who were doing that shooting as you ran along; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it was apparent to you as you ran along that you were in grave danger of being shot at any second; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you went to your hiding place, you were still able to hear this shooting going on around the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And indeed at all times when you were lying in that hiding spot, you could hear this shooting going on all around the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you've then given an account of what you can now remember of the conversation you heard on the road near to your hiding spot, and I just want to ask you this -- this question: You've done your best to tell the truth about what you heard in this Court; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. You have -- well, it's really a proposition and I'll ask you to agree or disagree. You have made a genuine effort to tell the truth about what you heard while you lay in your hiding spot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Now, I have some very brief questions about what you saw when you came out. I'm not going to take you back to the photographs, but I have to ask you these questions. When you saw the sad sight of your brother and sister and mother killed, the drawing that you drew indicated that the bodies were very near to each other. Now I just want to ask you about that. Were the bodies very near to each other as you've indicated there -- perhaps I'll ask it this way. Were the bodies within a foot or two feet of each other when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, perhaps it was a bit more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. But generally speaking, you were satisfied with the accuracy of the positions that you drew on that photograph that has been tendered in evidence here in Court; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, that is more or less so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Just excuse me please one moment, Mr. Zelic. Mr. Zelic, I'm just considering now if I have any more questions. If you just permit me a moment to consider this matter, I'll -- we'll be finished very shortly. Yes, there are two residual questions and then I've finished. The first one concerns whether you recognised any of the voices that you heard on the road, of the people who were speaking there? Of course you recognised your family, but of the men who were speaking while you were in your hiding spot.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As to Janja Grubesa, did you understand Janja Grubesa to be a person who regularly cooked for the soldiers in the HVO in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To your understanding, in September of 1993, did Janja Grubesa cook for the HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, she worked in the kitchen. I cannot tell you whether, on that precise day, she was working in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of course not. But by -- when you say "the kitchen," do you mean a kitchen that was based at the school or nearby to the school?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in the school. As far as I can recall, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just to be quite clear, that was a kitchen which provided meals for the on-duty HVO soldiers who needed food while at frontline positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did your mother also work, from time to time, at that kitchen?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, ever observe Janja Grubesa with a firearm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Zelic, thank you for answers my questions as you have. That's the end of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No redirect examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Judge El Mahdi, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Witness, one point of clarification, please. You stated that your mother told you when you escaped from the house, she told you to go to the school. You said that you were the one who started running in the direction of the school but then you arrived next to the house of Ivan Zelenika. At that point, you started off towards the junction. Can you please explain to us why you decided to go in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because our soldiers were in the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but was Ivan's house on the way to the school, was it located on the way to the school?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when you go from my house toward the school, then his house it on the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And did you have to go through the junction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then why did you set off in that direction? Why didn't you go in that other direction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we saw that the stable was on fire. We saw a soldier and we assumed that there was something wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you take that decision on your own, the decision to change directions? Because if I understand you correctly, the other members of your family were behind you, about 10 metres behind you.

utterances.speaker: MARKO ZELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I changed the decision because we heard shooting and stables were burning and that would not have been done by Croatian soldiers. We knew it had to be done by the enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's question? I see none. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? It seems to me there is none. Yes, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your testimony. Madam Usher will show you out of the room and we wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I think Mr. Sachdeva has got an application to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours. I wish to make an application pursuant to Rule 75 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and Article 22 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Perhaps we can go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness. Would you please stand up and make the solemn declaration accordance with the paper that Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness H. The Tribunal has granted the Prosecution protection for Prosecution application for your protection and you are protected by way of facial distortion and pseudonym. Now, I'm going to show you a piece of paper with some details on them, and can you please tell the Court whether they are correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Might that be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P358 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session while I ask questions about his personal background?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness H, in 1993, who was the commander of the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Enver Buza.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where was the command headquarters of the Prozor Independent Battalion in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: For a time, it was in the village of Stipe and later on it was transferred to the Dobro Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: When was it transferred to Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when it was transferred, but I think it was in that year, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Dobro Polje was the command centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: What kind -- sorry, what kind of building was the command centre in Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: It was a wooden shack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph, Witness H.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I show the witness photograph 0402-0900.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness H, do you see a photograph on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it there now, Witness H?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can you see on that photograph the building where the command centre was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher to provide you with a pen. I'd like you to circle that building, if you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour I think there's a slight technical hitch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could ask some other questions tomorrow when we come back. You still have a chance to use these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Now, Witness H, did you ever visit the battalion command room in Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Where was your group situated, the military police group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Above the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: How far away from the command centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: About 50 to 100 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a village called Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Partly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now we have the picture on our screen. You may try it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Witness H, do you see the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Do you see that there's a red circle around a building there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Which building is that, just for the -- for clarity, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: It's the building where the headquarters was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Of the Prozor Independent Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: The command of the battalion, yes, the Independent Prozor Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Can I ask you to write the letter C above the circle, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS H
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that for admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original Prosecution Exhibit P359 and the one that's marked now Prosecution Exhibit P360.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Is it a good time to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, and we will resume tomorrow afternoon. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I just -- I had understood that we were going to start at 10.30 tomorrow morning. Is that not going to happen -- Friday, pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: On Friday, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Tomorrow afternoon. Witness, I believe that you have to stay in The Hague for another night, and you have to understand that you are under oath now. So please do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And when we adjourn, Madam Usher will pull down the blinds and she will show you out of this courtroom. And you just stay where you are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of April, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
